title: MetaDSE: A Few-shot Meta-learning Framework for Cross-workload CPU Design Space Exploration
problem: Cross-workload CPU design space exploration suffers from overfitting, data ambiguity, and workload dissimilarity when leveraging transfer learning.
motivation: Existing DSE methods require extensive target workload simulation; meta-learning can enable rapid adaptation to new workloads with minimal data.
method: MetaDSE reframes cross-workload CPU DSE as a few-shot meta-learning problem using model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML). It introduces a workload-adaptive architectural mask algorithm to uncover inherent architectural properties across diverse workloads.
key_novelty: Application of few-shot meta-learning with workload-adaptive architectural masking to enable rapid DSE adaptation across diverse CPU workloads.
contributions: Reformulation of CPU DSE as few-shot meta-learning problem to overcome overfitting and data ambiguity
Workload-adaptive architectural mask algorithm uncovering inherent architecture properties
44.3% reduction in prediction error compared to state-of-the-art transfer learning methods
Open-sourced framework enabling efficient cross-workload exploration
limitations: Evaluation limited to SPEC CPU 2017; applicability to broader workload types not thoroughly explored.
primary_theme: Few-shot meta-learning for efficient CPU design space exploration
